correctness.rationale: Use the finite Heyting residual a→b=max{z:a∧z≤b} in B_n plus k *new* points (Boolean top retained). For Boolean nonzero S and consequent T⊆[n], S→T is new top if S⊆T, else complement(S)∪T; for added antecedent t_i it equals consequent on Boolean elements and top on added t_j≥t_i. These yield all asserted materializer sets and their inclusion order (B_n without zero)⊕C_k, with n=1 exceptional chain. The failures disjointly count as 3^n−2^n, (2^n−1)(k−1), k(k−1)/2; limit with k/2^n→c gives 1/2+1/[2(1+c)^2]. Independent finite lattice residual enumerator tested 16 (n,k) cases n≤4,k≤4 and all 2080 ordered implication inputs, sample n=3,k=2 gives 27 failures of 100; full proof is symbolic.

originality.rationale: Bumpus–Kocsis define materializers and prove qualitative failure of a uniform satisfiability gap using the one-added-top Boolean construction. Their inspected sections do not provide the inclusion-order isomorphism for arbitrary attached chain length, the exact failure polynomial, or the scaling/limit noncommutation. Resultary finite-chain preconditional records use different operations, not this materializer family. Genuine prior special case k=1 is credited.

value.rationale: The inclusion poset recovers algebra parameters, a structural classification. Exact satisfaction probabilities and two noncommuting limiting regimes quantify the previously qualitative Boolean-top phenomenon and can serve as finite-Heyting benchmarks; this is not simply a renaming of k=1.
